anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of On Pascha exists (Toura 1941; Daly ACW 54 and Witte's German are copyrighted and were not copied). Sense checked against the locked Witte Greek (and, for 1.94, Victor of Capua's Latin as Witte prints it) and the wording of the cited scriptures.

apparatus: {δὲ} deleted. Insertions <ἀνδρὸς καὶ τοῦ>, τῆ<ς> θηλεία<ς>.

bible_refs.note: Loin and navel as the devil's hold, male and female.

choices.why: Origen marks that he is speaking of the woman's navel with reserve.

pass_a_gloss: For especially through this desire he is able both to turn inside-out and to wrestle down humans, the loin as of the man and the navel of the belly being decently understood as of the woman, so that it may be shown that through such desire he most of all prevails over both the male and the female.
pass_b_english: For especially through this desire he is able both to overturn and to wrestle down human beings — the loin being understood, as of the man, and the navel of the belly decently as of the woman — so that it may be shown that through such desire he most of all overpowers both the male and the female (Job 40:16).
source_text: [μά]λιστα γὰρ διὰ ταύτης τῆς ὀρέξεως καὶ ἐκστρέφειν καὶ καταπαλαίειν δυνατός ἐστιν τοὺς ἀν(θρώπ)ους, τῆς ὀσφύος ὡς {δὲ} ἐπὶ τοῦ <ἀνδρὸς καὶ τοῦ> ὀμφαλοῦ τῆς γασ[τ]ρὸς εὐσχημόνως ὡς ἐπὶ τῆ<ς> θ[η]λεία<ς> νοουμένων, ἵνα δηλωθῇ ὅτι διὰ τῆς τοιαύτης ὀρέξεως μάλιστα κατισχύει καὶ τὸν ἄρρενα καὶ τὴν θηλείαν.
